column1:
When and why do you use the
Pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo?
column2:
The past counterfactual — things that didn't happen, and regret about them.
  • Unreal conditions in the past — si hubiera sabido, habría ido.
  • Regret — ojalá no hubiera dicho nada.
  • Backshifted perfect subjunctive — no creía que hubiera terminado.
  • Como si in the past — actuaba como si no hubiera pasado nada.

column1:
Tricks and tips for the
Pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo
column2:
• Learn as one unit with the condicional compuesto: si hubiera sabido, habría ido.
  • Both halves may be hubiera — si hubiera sabido, hubiera ido is common and fully acceptable. The reverse (habría in the si clause) is not.
  • -se forms are equally valid: hubiese, hubieses, hubiese, hubiésemos, hubieseis, hubiesen.
  • Drill the whole sentence shape rather than the two tenses separately.
